title: Dali / Lhasa
hook: 1200 → 1700. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Dali / Lhasa in 1200 and 1700, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 1200 and 1700; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Dali area anchor: 100.27, 25.61 (0 km from the nominal location); Lhasa area anchor: 91.12, 29.65 (0 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 1200 and 1700 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["Nan Chao"],["Tibet"]],[["Post-Ming Warlords"],["Tibet"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1200.geojson (SHA-256 2d6913ecedb38e269e41d249c87874d81e3e8d7351754821f57e627442d91525); GeoJSON features [[26],[24]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1700.geojson (SHA-256 eb73d6b00e98205fb2082de050c35e4d698224b17849628d82584610186b88a4); GeoJSON features [[93],[56]]

claims.text: At the two points, 1200 has different labels and 1700 has different labels. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1200.geojson (SHA-256 2d6913ecedb38e269e41d249c87874d81e3e8d7351754821f57e627442d91525); GeoJSON features [[26],[24]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1700.geojson (SHA-256 eb73d6b00e98205fb2082de050c35e4d698224b17849628d82584610186b88a4); GeoJSON features [[93],[56]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: The same coordinate receives a different label in a later map. What must have moved? Answer: Nothing necessarily; the map classification changed A fixed coordinate can be classified differently without establishing migration or physical movement.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[9]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

recall.question: The same coordinate receives a different label in a later map. What must have moved?
options: Nothing necessarily; the map classification changed
recall.why: A fixed coordinate can be classified differently without establishing migration or physical movement.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
